title: Youth
story_excerpt: I never thought of it as fear. What I remember is wanting to get closer — the size of it, the noise, the sheer weight of the thing bearing down the rails, and somewhere underneath the wanting was an old plan to press a penny flat against the steel, to hold proof I'd stood that close. I didn't know the word for it then, but I understand it now: I wasn't running toward danger, I was running toward power, trying to touch something enormous enough to leave a mark on me — or let me leave one on it. Seventy years later I'm still doing it, just quieter. No tracks, no horn, no mother running to pull me back. Just the same boy, reaching for the biggest thing in the room to see what it's made of.
